title: Add traffic-shape-aware regression-fusion detector and rollout guard
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We continue to see spurious canary failures when traffic composition shifts sharply (cold start bursts, client-side A/B traffic shaping) even though core latency distribution for steady-state users remains stable. This PR implements a traffic-shape-aware regression fusion detector that reduces false positives by weighting metric signals by concurrent traffic percentile buckets and by fusing orthogonal detectors (latency percentile drift, request-rate-aware tail risk, and service-time quantile drift) with a probabilistic voting model. Summary of changes: 1) New fusion detector module src/detectors/traffic_fusion_detector.go — computes weighted quantile deltas per traffic-percentile slice, applies exponential smoothing, and outputs a composite regression score; 2) Rollout guard integration internal/guards/traffic_fusion_guard.go — ties detector output to canary policies with configurable thresholds, cooldowns, and auto-rollback windows; 3) Canary simulator test harness tests/canary_sim/traffic_shape_sim.go to reproduce bursty-shape scenarios and validate false-positive rate reduction; 4) Metrics and dashboards dashboards/perf/traffic-fusion.jsonnet and observability hooks in internal/metrics/exports.go; 5) CI/perf job adjustments .github/workflows/perf-canary.yml to include the new sim; 6) Documentation: docs/perf/canary-detectors.md updated with configuration knobs and recommended thresholds. Design notes: the detector buckets traffic by request size, client region, and user cohort signals when available, then computes per-bucket latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) and derives a weighted aggregate delta using traffic-weighted importance and recency decay. The fusion layer combines evidence from three independent heuristics and produces a calibrated p-value-like score that maps to guard action levels (monitor, warn, fail). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for detector internals - [x] Integration tests for guard + pipeline - [x] Canary sim scenarios covering skewed traffic shapes - [x] Dashboard + alerting wiring - [x] Performance budget: detector CPU < 3% of canary service on standard instance - [x] Backwards compatible config defaults Rollout and operational notes: default behavior is opt-in via canary config, recommended initial threshold is score>=0.85 to trigger a soft-fail with automated alerting and a 30m cooldown, we expect to tune based on canary traffic in first two weeks after rollout. Migration: no data migrations required, default configs preserve existing detection behavior until enabled. Risks and mitigations: false negatives for extremely low-volume cohorts — mitigated by a minimum-sample guard and an aggregated fallback detector; increased CPU consumption under extreme cardinality — mitigated by a cardinality cap with sampling. Testing and validation: local unit coverage 92%, CI integration job initially failed on a race in metrics exporter causing a flake, fixed by introducing a metrics export mutex and re-ran perf-e2e where the canary sim showed false-positive rate drop from ~6.4% to ~1.1% on historical noisy traces. Related work: follows up on ENG-2319 where per-percentile routing was proposed, and PERF-402 which prototyped multivariate detector fusion. Notes for reviewers: focus on detector calibration math in traffic_fusion_detector.go and the guard thresholds; new sim is intentionally deterministic and includes seeded randomness to make CI reproducible. Manual QA: ran canary against a synthetic service with injected 10% tail latency perturbation and verified guard escalations and rollbacks behave as documented.
commits: feat(detector): add traffic-shape-aware fusion detector implementation
test(sim): add canary traffic-shape simulator and e2e scenario harness
chore(ci): wire perf-canary job to run sim and publish artifact
fix(metrics): mutex export in observability hook to prevent flake
docs: add traffic-fusion usage and tuning guide
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: please add a short note about how we choose decay constants; suggest exposing as a knob in config and defaulting to 3 minutes — responded and added decay constants to defaults.go

Priya Nair: observed a potential O(N^2) in the bucketing step for high-cardinality client ids, requested a ceiling and sampling strategy — implemented a cardinality cap and added unit tests — author reply: added cap with graceful sampling and documented behavior

Liam O'Connor: can we measure detector CPU under high load? suggested a microbenchmark — added tools/bench/traffic_fusion_bench.go and included results in PR description; CI perf job shows CPU at ~2.2% of canary service under test
release_notes: Introduce a traffic-shape-aware regression fusion detector and an opt-in rollout guard. Reduces false-positive canary failures during skewed traffic patterns; opt-in via canary config. No breaking changes.
